startup.name: Asimov
startup.one_liner: Real-world human movement data for humanoid robots
startup.description: Collects real world human movement data in homes and businesses to train humanoid robots, selling diverse data to robotics labs. The input claims thousands of hours a day delivered to leading labs. Team of three in San Francisco.

yc_acceptance.basis: Starting prior is about 1 percent for a random applicant (0.6 to 2 percent range, references/yc_acceptance.md). Up for a claim of existing sales to leading labs (real usage factor) and for physical AI being a hot YC theme. Down because the team is three people, the buyer group is a few dozen labs and data collection is operationally heavy. Net about 4 percent, conditional on the batch already given.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most likely say that the customer base is a handful of well funded labs that can collect data themselves, that research suggests human video can substitute for expensive robot data but pricing is unproven, and that data collection firms are multiplying. Partners may doubt a three person team can manage privacy, labeling and scale.

Time table era 2022+: seed p25 3, median 6, p75 14 months; series_a p25 19.4, median 28 months from batch start; Industrials median months to seed 6 (stage_benchmarks.md).
anchors.adjustment_reason: Window is 10.4 months from 2026-01-05 to 2026-11-17 and the number is for a round above about 1M from outside investors that closes inside it. Anchor 0.59 B2B and 0.74 Industrials (anecdote, n=19); 0.50 is 0.85x of the B2B anchor because only part of the seeds close within 10 months. Robotics data is a hot area but the winners test says not to lift above the anchor for a hot sector. These odds do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round under 3M, likely if revenue is concentrated in one or two labs.
Typical institutional seed near the 2022 and later median of 4.1M.
Strong seed from a robotics or AI fund if lab contracts are real and recurring.
Large seed in the physical AI category, where recent raises were large; rare for three people.

ladder.why_it_fails: The seed step fails if the claimed lab revenue is a few pilot orders, if labs build in house or buy from larger data vendors, or if investors see data collection as a services business with low margins. K-Scale Labs shut down in humanoids without a post YC round, and Sensei, Cortex AI and Almond show a crowd of robotics data and robot companies, most with no priced round found.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series C in the first year after the batch has no precedent. It would require the humanoid market itself to arrive at scale and this company to hold a dominant share of its training data, while the labs and large data vendors compete for that position.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most likely a stall as buyers consolidate and in house collection or cheaper egocentric video from the internet substitute; or a sale to a larger data or robotics company for under 100M. The upside requires humanoid robots to reach deployment and this company to be the standard data supplier, a bet on the whole category. K-Scale shows that humanoid companies can die quickly.

killers.mitigation: Sign multi year data contracts and add new buyer types.

killers.risk: Labs collect in house or buy from larger vendors

killers.mitigation: Compete on diversity of environments and privacy compliant collection.

killers.risk: Privacy, consent and operations in homes
killers.evidence: Recording in households raises consent and regulatory issues and heavy operational cost for three people.
killers.mitigation: Build consent flows and bounded geographies.

killers.evidence: Humanoid companies depend on future robot sales; K-Scale Labs shut down early.
killers.mitigation: Serve non humanoid robotics and AI labs too.

technical_complexity.rationale: Capturing wearable video and motion data at scale is feasible with cameras and phones. The hard parts are consent, quality control, labeling at the density robot learning needs and logistics across many homes. A three person team can run a pilot, but scale needs operations and tooling.

takeover_risk.rationale: Larger data vendors can add physical data collection within a year, and labs can collect themselves. Switching costs for datasets are low, but diversity of real homes is hard to copy quickly.

evidence.claim: Research shows pretraining on human egocentric video improves humanoid success rates, which creates demand for diverse data.
A data ecosystem for humanoid training is forming, but market size figures come mostly from vendors.

brand.name: Asimov
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Asimov" --era 2022+: invented or proper name, 6 characters, 3 syllables, no descriptor.
strengths: Evokes robotics through the Three Laws author
weaknesses: Common name that may be shared by other companies
brand.rationale: A proper name that signals robots helps recall with robotics buyers and investors, in the way that names such as Anduril or Palantir borrow from literature. Brand is secondary to buyer demand.

narrative.headline: Hot sector and claimed lab sales, but a three person team selling to a few buyers: about even odds of a 1M plus round in 10 months.
narrative.general_summary: Asimov sells real world human movement data to robotics labs. The need is plausible from research, but buyers are few and rivals multiply. The window is 10.4 months from 2026-01-05 to 2026-11-17 and the seed number is for a round above about 1M. The B2B anchor is 59 percent ever and the forecast is 0.50 since only part of seeds close inside 10 months and a hot sector is not lifted per the winners test. Series A inside the window is unlikely. The odds do not rank this company against others.

assumptions: Blind forecast as of 2026-01-05 using only the input; the delivery claim is unverified.
Seed means above about 1M from outside investors inside the 10.4 month window.
Same period robotics data comps were not used for outcomes.
